b: My 5-year-old was supposed to attend a classmate’s birthday party this weekend, which I ultimately didn’t let her attend, and now I feel like I made the wrong decision.

For background, my wife and I have set very firm boundaries with our kids and explained that hitting is not a solution to a problem. In this case, my 5-year-old had a meltdown when I wouldn’t let her buy something while running errands, which led to slapping and kicking me in the face, along with running off on her own in the middle of a busy store. This to me was one of those moments where I felt like she had to learn a tough lesson, which is why I didn’t let her go, but now I’m feeling awful about my decision. I feel like I ended up punishing her classmate by not letting my daughter attend, and now I’m wondering if the punishment fit the behavior or if I should have approached the situation differently.

Would love to hear other parents’ thoughts on this. Did I overreact? Should I have chosen a different kind of punishment? I feel so awful right now and offered to reimburse the parents for my daughter’s spot at the party.
